prompt.context: Complete Foods, a leading supermarket prominent across the U.S., is planning to release a private label line of paper towels. They currently sell fresh and shelf-stable grocery products as well as some common household items such as hand soap and kitchen supplies. Some of these products are brand names and some are private label. The CMO has asked your team to think through the pricing strategy for the new line.
prompt.question: How should Complete Foods price its new private label paper towel line?

clarifying_info.q: How many stores does Complete Foods have?
clarifying_info.a: Complete Foods has 50 stores across 10 metropolitan areas, scattered across the United States.

clarifying_info.q: What kinds of products does Complete Foods currently sell?
clarifying_info.a: They sell fresh and shelf-stable grocery products as well as common household items such as hand soap and kitchen supplies — some brand name, some private label.
Complete Foods only stocks products that are free from artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives.
Last year, Complete Foods brought in revenue of $200M.

clarifying_info.q: Does Complete Foods already produce private label products?
clarifying_info.a: Complete Foods already produces private label grocery products but no private label household goods.

clarifying_info.q: What does private label mean in this context?
clarifying_info.a: Private label means products produced by the same company that is selling them. These paper towels will be produced by Complete Foods and only sold in Complete Foods stores.

exhibits.title: Paper Towels Market Landscape
exhibits.shows: A scatterplot of four brands currently sold at Complete Foods, plotting Brand Perception Score (x-axis, scale 0–4.5) against Price per 75-sheet two-ply roll (y-axis, $0–$5.00). Dot sizes are all equal. The x-axis label notes scores come from a third-party CPG industry survey; the y-axis is limited to 75-sheet two-ply rolls.

data.note: Two brands cluster at lower price and lower brand perception score; two brands cluster at higher price and higher brand perception score. Exact coordinates are read from the chart.

exhibits.title: Paper Towel Production Cost Options
exhibits.shows: A table listing three paper producers with their production cost per sheet and quality rating.

framework: Competitors: Who are the other brand-name competitors at Complete Foods? What are their price points? How might they react to a new private label brand on the shelf (potential lost sales)?

Company: What is Complete Foods concerned about? — cost of supplies (paper, cardboard, plastic), number of varieties to offer, supply chain (establishing a new household-goods supply chain separate from grocery), and sourcing (new supplier relationships).
Customers: What is the total market size for paper towels? What is the price elasticity? Do customers care about non-artificial ingredients in paper towels?

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, where should Complete Foods position its private label paper towel in the market?
questions.guidance: The candidate should observe that there are two clusters: two lower-priced, lower-perception brands and two higher-priced, higher-perception brands. There is a gap in the middle — a mid-range price and mid-range brand perception — where Complete Foods' private label can fit. The candidate should conclude the brand should target a moderately priced, medium-quality position between the two clusters. After identifying the positioning, they should move to estimating costs and a markup to recommend a specific price.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 and additional information provided by the interviewer, calculate the recommended retail price per roll for the new private label paper towel.
questions.guidance: The candidate should: (1) focus only on medium or high-quality suppliers since the brand targets mid-range quality; (2) multiply cost-per-sheet by 75 to get paper cost per roll; (3) add packaging cost per roll; (4) add shipping cost per roll; (5) apply the 30% industry markup. The interviewer should reveal packaging and shipping tables and the 30% markup only when asked. The candidate should select the cheapest options among medium/high quality. An advanced candidate may note that speed or reliability of shipment companies is not reflected in the cost data.

math.setup: 75-sheet roll. Focus on medium-quality paper (BB or CC). Choose cheapest packaging and shipping among medium/high quality. Apply 30% industry markup (multiply total cost by 1.3).
steps: Paper Producer BB cost per roll: $0.035 x 75 = $2.625
Paper Producer CC cost per roll: $0.040 x 75 = $3.00
Select cheapest shipping: Shipment Company HH at $0.025/roll
Add packaging — Producer DD (HIGH, $0.19) or EE (MEDIUM, $0.16); choose EE as cheapest medium/high quality:
BB + HH + EE: $2.65 + $0.16 = $2.80 (note: casebook shows $0.15 for EE in the worked example, yielding $2.80)
Recommended combination (cheapest medium-quality path): BB + HH + EE = $2.80
math.answer: Recommended retail price: $3.64 per 75-sheet two-ply roll

brainstorming.prompt: What other considerations outside of price should Complete Foods think about when introducing a new product line into their stores?

categories.name: Internal considerations
ideas: Making shelf space for the product in stores
Ability to make other products with the same value chain (toilet paper, printing paper, etc.)

categories.name: External considerations
ideas: Impact on ordering quantities from competing brands now that there is an additional brand on the shelf

recommendation: Complete Foods should introduce its private label paper towel at approximately $3.64 per 75-sheet two-ply roll, positioning it in the mid-range on both price and brand perception — filling the gap between the two lower-tier and two higher-tier brands currently sold in stores.

This price is derived from using Paper Producer BB (medium quality, $0.035/sheet x 75 = $2.625/roll), Shipping Company HH ($0.025/roll), and Packaging Producer EE (medium quality, ~$0.15–$0.16/roll), totaling ~$2.80 in landed cost, then applying the 30% industry markup.
risks: Manufacturers may not be able to support the volume that Complete Foods is requesting.
There may be unassessed differences among suppliers, such as shipment speed or reliability.
Competitors may be upset that the brand is moving into their product line and taking up shelf space.
next_steps: Get additional data points from suppliers to continue differentiating and ensure reliable service.
Start planning shelf space agreements with existing brands.
Start working on marketing and sales plans for the new private label line.
